title: Valid Word
constraints: word contains only English uppercase and lowercase letters, digits, '@', '#' and '$'
notes:
## Intuition

Each rule is a simple fact about the string, so a single scan can collect everything: whether any forbidden character appears, whether a vowel appears, and whether a consonant appears. The length rule needs no scan at all, so check it first.

## Approach

1. If `word` has fewer than 3 characters, return `false`.
2. Start with `hasVowel` and `hasConsonant` both `false`.
3. For each character `ch`: skip digits, since they are allowed but count as neither kind.
4. Otherwise take its lowercase form `lower`. If it is not a letter from `a` to `z` (here that means `@`, `#` or `$`), return `false` at once.
5. Mark `hasVowel` if `lower` is one of `aeiou`, otherwise mark `hasConsonant`.
6. After the scan, return `hasVowel && hasConsonant`.

## Example 1, step by step

`word = "234Adas"` has 7 characters, so the length rule passes. `'2'`, `'3'` and `'4'` are digits and are skipped. `'A'` becomes `'a'`, a vowel, so `hasVowel = true`. `'d'` is a consonant, so `hasConsonant = true`. `'a'` and `'s'` change nothing new. No forbidden character appeared and both flags are set, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over `word`.
- Space: O(1): two flags.

## Pitfalls

- Uppercase vowels count too: `"UPPERCASE"` is valid. Lowering each letter before the vowel test handles this.
- `y` is a consonant, not a vowel.
- Digits are allowed but are neither vowels nor consonants, so `"123"` is invalid.
- A forbidden symbol makes the word invalid even if the other rules hold, wherever it appears.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `hasVowel` | whether a vowel has been seen |
| `hasConsonant` | whether a consonant has been seen |
| `ch` | the current character |
| `lower` | `ch` in lowercase, used for the letter and vowel tests |

narration.2: A valid word needs at least 3 characters; check this before scanning.
narration.3: Too short, so it cannot be valid.
narration.5: No vowel has been seen yet.
narration.6: No consonant has been seen yet.
narration.8: Digits are allowed but are neither vowels nor consonants...
narration.9: ...so move on to the next character.
narration.11: Lowercase the character so one test covers both cases.
narration.12: Anything that is not a letter at this point is a forbidden symbol.
narration.13: One forbidden character makes the whole word invalid.
narration.15: Is the letter one of the five vowels?
narration.16: Record that a vowel was found.
narration.18: Every other letter is a consonant; record it.
narration.21: Valid only if both a vowel and a consonant appeared.
